I liked detailed anecdotes because they leak information. One persons "highschool" bullying anecdote might leak that they resented school because it tried to learn you shit like quadratic equations and history. Maybe the bullying part is made up, but one can be pretty sure that indirect testimony about the student not seeing the point of school is true.

Meanwhile, some-one else is directly complaining about the useless of the content of the lessons. Quadratic equations, history, bunk. They let slip that the bullies would force the nerds to do their homework for them. Since the bullying wasn't the point of anecdote, that part of the tale is probably being told straight.

Putting things together, the line that one person is pushing in their anecdote is often confirmed or refuted by what leaks from somebody else's anecdote pushing a different line.
